Description:
Tangency type 4: contact along an edge or at a single vertex. Unlike types 1 to 3 this splits into two groups that need separate treatment, because an edge or vertex contact does not necessarily mean the bodies merely touch:
GROUP 1, contact only (a to e): the bodies share an edge or a point but no volume. a two boxes sharing one full edge, b two boxes sharing a single corner, c two boxes sharing only part of an edge, d a cone whose apex sits exactly on a face, e the same cone with the apex 1 mm inside as a non-degenerate control.
GROUP 2, shared edge WITH genuine overlap (f and g): a cube rotated 45 degrees about one of its own edges. The rotation keeps that edge fixed, so the two cubes share it exactly while their volumes overlap substantially. f uses a shortened cube (y = 2..8) so the shared edge is the only degeneracy; g is the plain case where the whole cube is rotated, which additionally leaves the two pairs of end faces coplanar - a type 1 coincidence on top of the shared edge, and the configuration that occurs in practice.
The intersection area of a 10x10 square with itself rotated by 45 degrees about a corner is 100*(sqrt(2)-1) = 41.421356, which makes every expected volume in f and g exact.
Expected:
a, b, c: intersect empty; union two separate solids (the confirmed convention for bodies that meet in less than a face); difference unchanged, 1000 and, in c, 400.
d  cone from (5,5,10) to (5,5,14) with radii 0 and 3, apex exactly on the top face: V = 12*pi = 37.699112. intersect empty; union two solids; difference box-cone 1000; difference cone-box 37.699112.
e  CONTROL, the same cone with its apex at z=9, so it crosses the top face and 1 mm of it is inside the box. The submerged part is a cone of height 1 and radius 0.75: V = 3*pi/16 = 0.589049. intersect 0.589049; union 1000 + 12*pi - 3*pi/16 = 1037.110063; difference box-cone 999.410951.
f  cube (0,0,0)..(10,10,10) and a box (0,2,0)..(10,8,10) rotated 45 degrees about the y axis through the origin: intersect 600*(sqrt(2)-1) = 248.528137; union 1600 - 248.528137 = 1351.471863; difference A-B 751.471863; difference B-A 351.471863.
g  the same with the full cube: intersect 1000*(sqrt(2)-1) = 414.213562; union 1585.786438; difference 585.786438 in either direction, by symmetry.
Note on tolerances: a cone with a true apex triangulates poorly at the tip, so its volume comes out about 1.2e-4 relative below the exact value. Everything else in this file is exact to 1e-9 or better, boxes to the last bit.
Status:
PASSES (2026-08-13, after the change concerning non-manifold edges). Keep as a regression guard for tangency type 4. All 22 checks correct, and the three cases that once failed were repeated 8 times each without a miss - which matters here, because case g used to be correct on a single run about one time in three.

Earlier defects, both fixed, for the record:
DEFECT 1 - intersect returned EMPTY when the two solids share an edge and genuinely overlap. id 30 (intersect of fA and fB, the shortened rotated cube) failed 8 of 8 runs, id 37 (the full rotated cube) 6 of 8. The unions and differences on exactly the same operands (ids 32, 33, 39, 40) were always right, so the overlap itself was computed correctly and only the intersection discarded it. Two controls located it: moving the rotation axis off the shared edge by as little as 0.5 mm made the intersection work (283.16 at 0.5 mm, 316.76 at 1 mm, 380.88 at 2 mm), and the axis aligned analogue - box (0,0,0)..(10,10,10) intersected with box (0,0,0)..(5,5,20), sharing the edge x=0, y=0 and overlapping in 250 - was correct 4 of 4. So it took a shared edge where the faces meet at an oblique angle.
Two controls locate the trigger. Moving the rotation axis off the shared edge by as little as 0.5 mm makes the intersection work again (283.16 at 0.5 mm, 316.76 at 1 mm, 380.88 at 2 mm offset, all non-empty and of the right magnitude). And the axis aligned analogue - box (0,0,0)..(10,10,10) intersected with box (0,0,0)..(5,5,20), which share the edge x=0, y=0 and overlap in 250 - is correct on 4 of 4 runs. So neither the overlap nor a shared edge alone is enough: it takes a shared edge where the faces meet at an oblique angle.

DEFECT 2 (FIXED 2026-08-13) - a cone apex crossing a face used to break intersect AND difference. Case e returned the empty result for both, 8 of 8 runs, while the union of the same operands was correct at 1037.110062. An empty difference was the worse half: subtracting a cone that pokes 1 mm into the box must leave 999.410951, not nothing.
Two controls again. Replacing the true apex by a small flat - radii 0.1 and 3 instead of 0 and 3, same position - makes both operations correct (intersect 0.809600, difference 999.190386). And a cone with a true apex lying ENTIRELY inside the box works as well (difference 962.341773, intersect 37.694410). So it is neither the apex by itself nor the position by itself: it is a singular apex on a body that crosses a face of the other near that apex.
Actual (2026-08-13, current):
a: intersect empty, union 2 solids, difference 1000 (6 faces / 12 edges).
b: intersect empty, union 2 solids, difference 1000 (6/12).
c: intersect empty, union 2 solids, difference A-B 1000 (6/12), difference B-A 400 (6/12).
d: intersect empty, union 2 solids, difference box-cone 1000 (6/12), difference cone-box 37.694410 (3 faces / 6 edges).
e: intersect 0.589006 (3/6), union 1037.110062 (9/18), difference box-cone 999.410956 (8/18).
f: intersect 248.528137 (6/12), union 1351.471863 (12/28), difference A-B 751.471863 (11/25), difference B-A 351.471863 (7/15).
g: intersect 414.213562 (6/12), union 1585.786438 (8/18), difference 585.786438 (7/15) in both directions.
Repeated 8 times each: case f intersect, case g intersect, case e intersect, difference and union - no failure.
Actual (before the fixes): Case e: intersect empty and difference box-cone empty, both wrong, 8 of 8 runs, union already correct. Case f: intersect empty 8 of 8. Case g: intersect empty 6 of 8.
